newsitem.title: MEXICO: United, Mexicana airlines seen in code-share deal.
newsitem.headline: United, Mexicana airlines seen in code-share deal.

text.p: Mexican airline Mexicana de Aviacion and UAL Corp unit United Airlines plan to enter a code-sharing agreement, sources close to the deal said Thursday.
Fernando Flores, director general of Mexicana, and Chris Bowers, Senior Vice President International, plan to sign the agreement in a ceremony late Friday, the sources added.
The move would give Mexicana expanded access to destinations outside Mexico, and offer wider possibilities within Mexico to United.

The strategy could boost United's presence in Latin America and give the airline a leg up against competitor American Airlines, part of AMR Corp.. American recently announced an alliance -- subject to regulatory approval -- with British Airways Plc.

Analysts also said the move expands travel options with Mexicana, which had no previous code-sharing agreements. Its sister airline Aerovias de Mexico, known as Aeromexico, has code-sharing agreements with Delta Airlines and Air France.
Although Aeromexico and Mexicana stock is joined in holding company Cintra, the two companies are operated separately.
Code-sharing agreements offer mileage benefits and other pricing and flight options to flyers.
